pr_title: Require and preserve content type for filtered rest requests
pr_body:
`RestRequest#getXContentType` cannot normally be `null` for a request with
a non-empty request body, or the rest controll will reject the request, see eg
`RestControllerTests#testUnknownContentWithContentStream`.
This PR fixes sloppy behavior where the `RestRequestFilter` cleared the
`xContentType` field of the filtered request.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/84784
pr_comments: Hi @albertzaharovits, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: NPE when auditing REST requests with filtered fields
issue_context.body:
When auditing is configured to `emit_request_body` for REST requests, it can result into NullPointerException while trying to auditing the request body for a request that has filtered fields. 

A minimal reproduction:
```
// Audit log configuration

xpack.security.audit.enabled: true
xpack.security.audit.logfile.events.emit_request_body: true
xpack.security.audit.logfile.events.include: _all

// Create a User
PUT _security/user/foo
{"password":"password","roles":["superuser"]}
```

The above results into a 401 error with `null_pointer_exception` as its `caused_by`.

The problem is likely caused by #79814 which refactored how `RestRequest` is instantiated from another `RestRequest`. The new code does not set `xContentType` which means it is `null` and is rejected by `XContentHelper#converToJson`:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/987a83b93ef0f705dbdc5837c5a71c88f579a191/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/xcontent/XContentHelper.java#L310-L312
comments:

review_comments: I wonder if it is better to have separate tests that only focus on this copying constructor and content type being null?

I think a test for only the copy-constructor and the xContentType field would be too specific, and would not significantly improve coverage. Ideally, I would've tested the copy-constructor with the `equals` method on the `RestRequest` and also checked that the `xContentType` field (as well as the others) is part of that `equals` check.

But since there's no `equals` method in `RestRequest`, it made think of other ways to test: I noticed that there's the `RestControllerTests#testRestRequest` where I can introduce test coverage for the copy constructor; unfortunately that's not used in the xcontentType test, which got me to the current submission.
